text_nodes.text: Austin's order names six kinds of equipment.
The city manager is directed to acquire, deploy and activate it. The list is not limited to them. One property is written out of two of the six it names.
A plan is ordered. Its basis is on file.
The implementation plan has to rest on a July 2025 security audit the parks department already had done.
The resolution says what the plan must establish. The plan itself is not in it.
What the plan has to establish
RESOLUTION 20260812-017 / read in full, both pages
"Parks with a history of violent crime shall be prioritized for the initial deployment of this equipment." The mount is bare.
April had already listed the tools.
Artificial intelligence or machine learning tools sit among what is not permitted in City Code Chapter 2-19. The exception is whatever the city's own policy allows.
CITY CODE 2-19-9 NOT PERMITTED (B) ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE
The clause reaches the foot of the resolution's first page.
intelligence to conduct surveillance or analysis.

The clause finishes at the top of page two. It reaches a camera or drone that depends on artificial intelligence to do those two things. April had already listed those tools as not permitted. That listing carries an exception and this clause carries none.
